question: What does 0x6097630 do - the S0 writer behind the delimiter pre-step 0x6098510?
resolves: #4334 open unknown: 0x6097630 internals (the S0 writer behind the delimiter pre-step)

0x6097630.role: options-map serializer: walks the Configurable object's option-group range and appends name=value pairs into the output string S0
0x6097630.signature: (Status* out, const ConfigOptions* opts, const Configurable* object, const std::string* prefix, std::string* out_text)
0x6097630.returns: void; the final Status is written into *out

0x6098510.role: delimiter pre-step: truncates S0 to empty, forwards (out, object, C1, empty prefix string, S0) to 0x6097630, returns out
0x6098510.signature: (Status* out, const Configurable* object, const ConfigOptions* opts, std::string* s0)

0x60985e0.role: reset-and-serialize wrapper: resets *S to an empty SSO string, calls 0x6097630 with a stack Status temp (discarded, message freed), forwards its own rcx as the prefix, returns S
0x60985e0.signature: (std::string* out_text, const Configurable* object, const ConfigOptions* opts, const std::string* prefix)

0x60bb9a0.role: per-entry serializer (cited from #4311/#4320, not re-shipped): (Status* out, const OptionTypeInfo* record, const ConfigOptions* opts, const std::string* name, const void* options_base, std::string* value_out)
0x60bb9a0.note: record+0xac verification 4 skips the entry in the dump; every other verification serializes normally

iteration.range: object+0x08 begin, object+0x10 end (Configurable object: vtable at +0x00)
iteration.element_stride: 0x30 bytes; cursor += 0x30 at 0x6097690, end check against object+0x10

element_layout.+0x20: options-base pointer (passed to the serializer as its 5th argument; field address = base + record+0x00)
element_layout.+0x28: pointer to the per-group OptionTypeInfo map (null -> skip the element)

map.layout: unordered_map<string, OptionTypeInfo>, 56 bytes (same layout as #4334: buckets +0x00, bucket_count +0x08, before_begin +0x10, element_count +0x18)

skip_rules.note: the map-level dump drops verification-5 entries too; the bare serializer 0x60bb9a0 drops only verification 4 (0x60bb9d4)

skip_rules.condition: ConfigOptions+0x04 != 0 and record+0xd9 bit 0 clear and type not in {21, 22}
type in {21, 22} and ConfigOptions+0x28 != 2 and record+0xd9 bit 7 set

block_b.copy: full 0x50-byte ConfigOptions copy at 0x110(%rsp); copy+0x04 written 1 at 0x6097bdf then 0 at 0x6097ca7, so the serializer receives the copy with +0x04 == 0
block_b.shared_ptr: copy+0x48 refcount bumped (plain addl at 0x6097c92, or lock addl at 0x6098118 when the 0x64ed290 flag byte is 0); released after the call (xadd -1 at 0x6098263; count reaching 1 calls 0x5d35070, then the 0x6098298 path calls vtable slots 0x10 and 0x18)

block_c.condition: ConfigOptions+0x04 != 0, record+0xd9 bit 0 clear, type in {21, 22}, and (ConfigOptions+0x28 == 2 or record+0xd9 bit 7 clear)

serializer_calls.args: (Status@0x80(%rsp), record at node+0x28, ConfigOptions, name temp, options_base element+0x20, value_out T2@0x90(%rsp))
(Status@0x80(%rsp), record at node+0x28, copied ConfigOptions, name temp, options_base element+0x20, value_out T2@0x90(%rsp))
(Status@0x80(%rsp), record at node+0x28, ConfigOptions, name temp, options_base element+0x20, value_out T2@0x90(%rsp))

name_temp: prefix string (arg4) + name (node+0x08 data, node+0x10 length), built into a stack string before each serializer call

status.layout: 16-byte Status: bytes +0..+5 copied verbatim, pointer at +8; byte +0 is the code (0 = kOk)
status.error_propagation: serializer Status byte 0 != 0 -> the 6 bytes + pointer are copied into *out at 0x6097e6f..0x6097ea4 and the function returns immediately; later entries are not visited
status.empty_range: begin == end at entry (0x6097684..0x6097689) or the cursor reaching end -> *out is zeroed (16 bytes, 0x609827a..0x6098292) and the function returns (kOk)

emission.gate: value string T2 non-empty (T2.size at 0x98(%rsp) != 0, 0x60978cf); empty value -> nothing is appended for the entry
emission.format: prefix + name + "=" + value + delimiter, appended to S0 (arg5)
emission.delimiter: ConfigOptions+0x08 string (data at 0x8(%r15), length at 0x10(%r15)); slot 9 forces it to "; " (0x4409b0, 2 chars) when ConfigOptions+0x00 byte 0 == 0

wrappers.prefix_in_practice: both known call paths pass an empty prefix string (0x6098510 builds an empty temp; 0x609e510 builds an empty temp at 0x50(%rsp))

literals.role: name/value separator appended in the emission block
delimiter forced into the ConfigOptions copy by slot 9 when ConfigOptions+0x00 byte 0 == 0

open_unknowns: Element +0x00..+0x18 fields and the element struct's C++ name.
The map's C++ name: layout matches unordered_map<string, OptionTypeInfo> (before_begin +0x10, node key +0x08 / value record +0x28), but the node hash offset and total node size are not verified.
Why block B writes 1 then 0 to the copy's +0x04 byte (0x6097bdf, 0x6097ca7); only the end state (+0x04 == 0 at the call) is pinned.
0x609e510 host identity (FDE 0x609e510..0x609f073); it calls both 0x6098510 (0x609e80f) and 0x60985e0 (0x609e0a9).
What the release helper 0x5d35070 does exactly (cited only, from the block-B shared_ptr release path).
Slot-9 arg5 C++ meaning (still open from #4334).
ConfigOptions+0x00/+0x04/+0x08/+0x28 C++ names and defaults (still open from #4334).
